// Probe for the workflows-are-deterministic depguard rule.
//
// This file is NOT in the build graph — testdata/ is invisible to the Go tool,
// and the .txt suffix keeps it invisible to golangci-lint too. That is
// deliberate: a package whose only purpose is to fail lint would itself need a
// lint exclusion, which is the same hole one layer down that
// determinism_test.go exists to close.
//
// It is here because determinism_test.go asserts the TEXT of the rule, and the
// only way to check the EFFECT is to run the linter against workflow code that
// calls Render. Reconstructing this file is otherwise a research task for
// whoever next has to verify that the rule fires — it was one for the reviewer
// of #370.
//
// To check the effect, from the software-factory repository root:
//
//	mkdir -p internal/workflows
//	cp internal/prompts/testdata/workflow_probe.go.txt internal/workflows/probe.go
//	golangci-lint run ./internal/workflows/... 2>&1 | grep -c workflows-are-deterministic   # want 1
//	rm -rf internal/workflows
//
// The last line matters: leaving the probe behind makes every later lint run
// fail, and committing it is the exclusion problem above.
//
// It is the invisible case on purpose. It imports nothing on any deny list
// except internal/prompts, takes an injected renderer, and reads as pure
// orchestration — no time.Now, no rand, no I/O. Nothing but depguard can see
// that Render mints a fresh nonce and therefore returns different bytes on a
// Temporal replay than it did on the original execution.

package workflows

import (
	"github.com/0x63616c/software-factory/internal/prompts"
	"github.com/0x63616c/software-factory/internal/work"
)

// RenderInWorkflow is what a workflow author would plausibly write, and what
// must never lint clean.
func RenderInWorkflow(renderer *prompts.Renderer, ticket work.TicketDetail) (string, error) {
	return renderer.Render(prompts.Input{Stage: work.StagePlan, Ticket: ticket})
}
